newsitem.title: SPAIN: Iberia will not ditch Viasa, only seeks new partner.
newsitem.headline: Iberia will not ditch Viasa, only seeks new partner.

text.p: Spain's Iberia said on Wednesday that although it was looking for a new partner to take responsibilty for the management of Viasa, it would not abandon the troubled Venezuelan airline.
Iberia and Venezuela's Investment Fund (FIV) reached an agreement on a plan late on Tuesday to save the loss-making airline from bankruptcy.
"There are no names in mind as yet, we have just agreed that we will have a new operator....Iberia will stick with Viasa though," a spokesman from Iberia said.
Under the agreement, Viasa will no longer have a single president and Iberia and the FIV will share the responsibility for managing the airline, each with representatives within Viasa.
Iberia would not comment on the size of the stake the new operator may take in Viasa.
Iberia said on Wednesday it was now up to workers to accept the latest restructuring plan to save Viasa from bankruptcy.
Iberia, which owns 45 percent of Viasa, reached an agreement late on Tuesday with Venezuela's Investment Fund (FIV) to revive the loss-making airline.
"Now it's up to the workers to agree the conditions of the plan which includes a reduction of between 15 and 20 percent of the total workforce," said an Iberia spokesman.
"We will be back to square one if it is rejected...this viability plan is the only means we have now to avoid bankruptcy," he added.
A shareholders' meeting has been scheduled for either January 31 or February 8, depending on the timing of the workers' decision, he added.
Iberia said the agreement broadly mirrored a previous plan presented in November which workers rejected after the FIV withdrew its commitment to fund job cuts.

Under the latest proposal, the FIV will pour $18 million into the airline to fund the job cuts and a further $4-5 million for operational improvements together with around $1.5 million for tax reductions.
"All in all, the FIV will invest around $25 million...Iberia will place more or less the same amount of money," an Iberia spokesman said.
Iberia said it had agreed to capitalise a large portion of its debt with Viasa and reduce interest payments on the rest, without demanding a greater stake in the airline.
In the meantime, Iberia will take control of a part of Viasa's fleet which it was previously holding as guarantee for the debt. The planes will, however, remain operational under the Viasa banner.
The plan also foresees the freezing of wages and a suspension of unprofitable routes.
Iberia said with the FIV's backing, workers would be more likely to agree the plan.
"This agreement means that the workers will be covered now according to the original plan," said Iberia.
